original_title_field: Quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures of negative regularity for fractional nonlinear Schrödinger equations
outcome: Two confirmed core proof defects and six groups of local corrections; no established counterexample to the main quasi-invariance theorem
summary: The exact acquired arXiv2205.11453v1 was fully read and visually checked. A positive-probability finite-block construction disproves the scalar-kernel domination of a time-shifted random operator. Independent exact Galerkin differentiation disproves the transported-density formula under the paper's own covariance. These break essential local-estimate and density-bootstrap derivations. Density normalization has a consistent fixed-factor repair; a replacement phase-resolved operator proof is not certified. Six further groups give exact local corrections. Parameter elimination agrees with the printed threshold.
limitations: No counterexample to Theorem1.1 or to the final Proposition3.6 operator-moment statement is established. The exactfalse domination step anditsessentialdependenciesare established.
The density algebra can be repaired without altering fixedGaussianlaw or scalarparameterthreshold, but the randomoperator time-translation proof requires a replacement not supplied here.

problems_checked.P1: Confirmed Major for the false scalar-kernel domination, not the final Proposition3.6 moment theorem. For alpha2,s2/5,sigma0,q2,b3/8,b_prime1/3,r48, all printed parameter inequalities hold. At n3=-1,n4=1, Gaussian support on +/-10,+/-12 leaves exactly (12,10) and(-10,-12), with equal denominators and opposite phases +/-10736. Coefficients1 and-1 cancel the displayed scalar kernel, while temporal test windows select only one translated g input, giving nonzero output. Neighborhoods yield failure on positive probability sets for any fixed implicit domination constant. The energy kernel repeats the same error with its sign factor. The core local/lifespan/energy dependencies were traced. No replacement translation-aware random operator bound, nor main-theorem counterexample, is established.
problems_checked.P2: Confirmed Major. The explicitly declared complex Gaussian has real/imaginary variances1/2, hence finite-mode density exp(-W). Direct differentiation gives W_dot=-2 Im A and Q_printed=4 Im A. Volume preservation and backward change of variables therefore give the true transported density exp[-(1/2) integral Q_printed(Phi_-r u)dr], whereas the printed formula is its inverse square. The finite admissible witness alpha2,s1/2,gamma4,N1,z_-1=z_0=1,z_1=i has A=2i(1-sqrt2), so the discrepancy is nonzero, persists on an open Gaussian set, and satisfies the strict later parameter conditions. The conserved mass weight does not cancel it. Correcting sign/factor preserves fixed-constant absolute estimates but does not repair P1.
problems_checked.P3: Confirmed Minor by the adapted deterministic zero-mode drift. For F=lambda Re(v_hat(0)), all required moments hold and the left side equals -lambda^2/4; the printed cost1/2 gives infimum -lambda^2/2. Cost1 with the same drift map corrects it. The resulting stronger negative quadratic penalty still implies the later weakened upper bound, so no threshold failure is inferred from this coefficient alone.
problems_checked.P4: Confirmed Minor. The asserted H^s support fails since its squared norm is the almost surely divergent sum of independent |g_n|^2. The correct subcritical support already appears in the body. Wick-tail variance is sum<n>^-4s=O(N^(1-4s)); chaos comparison gives Lp rate N^(1/2-2s), tending to zero. The printed growing upper bound is not itself treated as false, only its use to infer Cauchy convergence is unsupported until this repair.
problems_checked.P5: Confirmed both local defects after a documented primary quantifier-reading recovery. The cutoff chi_[-T,T] is incompatible with a restriction norm on[0,T]: a nonzero smooth negative-time-supported mode has zero restriction norm and nonzero cutoff norm. The actual additional zero-trace range is -1/q<b_prime<=b<1+1/q_prime, so q=p2,b_prime0,b1/2 IS admissible. Independently rederived the smooth zero-trace family f_N-f_M, T=1/N,M=exp(N^2): f_N(0)=f_M(0)=1; global H1/2 norm is O((log N)^-1/2), whereas its L2(0,T) norm is at least c sqrt(T), contradicting the asserted sqrt(T) gain. The primary initially misread the lower bound, made a transient edit, then actual original-resolution image/text checks and bounded native recheck disproved that reading. All transient bytes and commands are retained; original current report/evidence were restored exactly. No incorrect withdrawal remains current. Strict downstream Duhamel exponents and one-sided cutoff repair delimit Minor severity.
problems_checked.P6: Confirmed Minor at the allowed p1. With alpha2,s2/5,q2,sigma3=0,N=4M,T=(1024M^4)^-1, the nonresonant triples(a,a+b,b),a<b in[M,2M], satisfy all truncation assumptions. Their positive third-chaos coefficients are at least c*T*M^-s, with c*M^2 orthogonal monomials and no cancellation. Hypercontractivity and interpolation give E||F||/T>=c*M^(3/5), contradicting a uniform CT first moment. The proof actually yields T^(p/2), and p52 uses exactly the repaired T^-1/2 normalization; no threshold loss follows.
problems_checked.P7: Confirmed Minor equation-convention defects. The plane wave u=e^(it) shows the printed gauge misses a factor2. The contraction functional omits the actual i*S Duhamel operator. The claimed uniform phase lower bound over alpha>1/2 fails for the near-equal-frequency second-difference family when alpha<1, while the main theorem uses alpha>1. Each correction was limited to its actual source convention and parameter scope.
problems_checked.P8: Confirmed Minor local continuation/bookkeeping defects. The correct cocycle adds S(t-1)V(u0)(1); the cubic time-shift subtraction uses S(t), not S(t0). The growth estimate needs1+||v||, witnessed by nonzero nonlinear remainder for u0=1,v=0; existing r>=1 absorbs this repair. An upper bound on -log of an exponential integral does not provide the needed integrability upper bound; the positive-log variational estimate does. The some-time event is weaker, not false; the required all-time event and localization exponent must be corrected. The terminal weak-L2 density and integer continuation argument remain conditional on true local/density bounds. Formal invariant-domain and final infinite-dimensional variational passage are not promoted from unresolved reconstruction limits into confirmed errors.
